summary: This bill authorizes grants to nonprofit health care facilities and home health agencies to pay essential workers up to $13 per hour in hazard pay (capped at $25,000 per worker per year) plus safety measures like PPE during any declared emergency or disaster.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a new federal grant program under the Public Health Service Act, authorizing 'such sums as may be necessary' for emergency hazard pay and safety measures to health care facilities. This directly expands federal outlays with no offsets or reductions mentioned.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue measures.

The legislation provides federal grants to public and private nonprofit health care facilities specifically to compensate essential health care workers during emergencies. This increases federal involvement in supporting the healthcare workforce rather than relying solely on market-based mechanisms.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration policy, visas, border security, or immigrant protections.
No provisions address reproductive health services, abortion access, or related regulations.
No provisions concern military or defense spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation.
The bill targets compensation for employed essential health care workers during disasters rather than expanding or altering means-tested welfare programs such as SNAP or TANF.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill authorizes new federal spending without revenue increases or spending cuts elsewhere, implicitly accepting additional deficit spending.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill mandates additional hazardous duty compensation and safety protections for essential health care workers, directly enhancing worker compensation and safeguards in hazardous conditions.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
